Talk/Poster Title: Single-molecule CTCF occupancy and zinc-finger engagement states revealed by Fiber-seq
Abstract: CTCF and cohesin are major organizers of three-dimensional genome architecture. Cohesin extrudes chromatin loops, and DNA-bound CTCF acts as a directional boundary that can pause or retain cohesin. Yet CTCF sites are neither constitutively occupied nor perfectly impermeable to cohesin, making both CTCF binding and boundary activity probabilistic. The molecular determinants underlying these two layers of heterogeneity remain incompletely understood. Here, we analyze Fiber-seq, a single-molecule chromatin footprinting approach, to quantify CTCF occupancy and zinc-finger (ZF)-DNA engagement on individual native DNA molecules. We find that CTCF occupancy is jointly shaped by sequence affinity, CpG methylation, and local chromatin context, with allele-specific binding providing an internal validation of these determinants. Beyond occupancy, single-molecule protection patterns reveal recurrent CTCF ZF-DNA engagement states whose relative abundance varies across genomic loci and is influenced by local sequence context. Importantly, engagement-state composition provides additional information about RAD21 enrichment, insulation strength, and chromatin loop strength beyond CTCF occupancy. Together, these results establish two quantitative dimensions of endogenous CTCF binding: occupancy determines how frequently a CTCF barrier is present, whereas the DNA-engagement state of bound CTCF provides a second layer associated with its functional effectiveness as a cohesin boundary.

Talk/Poster Title: DeepPBS-AF3: Bridging structure- and sequence-based models of protein-DNA binding specificity with AlphaFold 3
Abstract: Predicting DNA-binding specificity of a transcription factor (TF) is a challenging yet essential task for understanding gene regulation. While sequence-based models utilize abundant high-throughput binding data, the diversity of protein folds and binding-associated conformational changes motivate approaches that use 3D structural information. Previous work, DeepPBS, addresses this by predicting binding specificity as a position weight matrix (PWM) directly from protein-DNA complexes, by encoding physicochemical and geometric interactions. Its training, however, is heavily limited by the scarcity of experimental TF-DNA co-crystal structures. Here, we introduce DeepPBS-AF3, which leverages AlphaFold 3 (AF3) to generate structural inputs for TFs that lack experimental complexes. This approach enables DeepPBS-AF3 to be trained on AF3-predicted complexes and extends its applicability to binding specificity prediction with sequence inputs. When trained on AF3-predicted structures, DeepPBS-AF3 demonstrates greater accuracy and generalizability over DeepPBS. Furthermore, we present a workflow that predicts binding specificity for a TF without a known binding DNA sequence. Together, our results establish structure prediction as a viable approach to overcome the scarcity of experimental structures in structure-based prediction of binding specificity, with potential extension to other applications such as predicting binding affinity and binding sites.

Talk/Poster Title: VHSeek: Biology foundation model-based virus representations revealing virus host associations
Abstract: Virus-host association prediction is fundamental to virus-related disease control and phage therapy, yet many existing tools require candidate-host genome sequences, which may be unavailable for some eukaryotic hosts or impractical to search at the scale of large virome studies. We present VHSeek, a supervised virus-host association predictor that integrates DNA- and protein-derived viral representations. VHSeek combines nucleotide representations from AIDO.DNA and protein representations from ESM2 to learn virus-host association patterns, and then transfers predictions through known host taxonomies from lower to higher ranks. During inference, VHSeek uses viral sequence data and known host taxonomies, without host sequence data. Compared with iPHoP, the state-of-the-art baseline evaluated in this study, VHSeek improves genus-level maximum F1 score (Fmax), Top-1 accuracy, and area under the precision--recall curve (AUPR) by 12%, 19%, and 27%, respectively. Confidence thresholding enables abstention and reduces false discoveries. On the processed IMG/VR v4.1 metagenomic collection, VHSeek expands effective host coverage from 36.5% to 64.5% using a validation-calibrated confidence threshold. VHSeek prioritizes candidate viruses and reservoir hosts with potential human health impacts, including multi-host hypotheses in which one virus may be associated with humans and additional hosts (e.g., Saboya virus with Homo sapiens and Culicidae) not currently captured in the dataset.
